#1794. How Arsenal could bank transfer windfall as Mauricio Pochettino eyes Manchester United signing

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal would be set to benefit if Manchester United moved to make Folarin Balogun an early signing of the Mauricio Pochettino era.

Monaco striker Balogun is one of a number of United States internationals who are already being linked with a potential switch to Old Trafford during the January transfer window after USA boss Pochettino agreed to replace Michael Carrick, along with the likes of Villarreal full-back Alex Freeman.

The Brooklyn-born frontman has thrived under Pochettino’s management, becoming one of the USA’s most important players and notching 12 goals in his first 31 senior caps after switching his international allegiance from England, who he previously represented from Under-17 to U21 level.

Balogun became a prominent figure at the past summer’s World Cup co-hosted by the USA, with the decision by FIFA’s disciplinary committee to suspend his one-match ban for a year following a sending off against Bosnia and Herzegovina in the last 32 proving massively controversial as he was able to play in the last-16 defeat by Belgium, with US President Donald Trump admitting that he asked FIFA to review the suspension.

Balogun, 25, rose through the youth ranks at Arsenal from the age of eight and spent time on loan at Middlesbrough and Reims before heading back to Ligue 1 with Monaco on a permanent basis in 2023, where he has since scored 32 goals and delivered 13 assists in 98 total appearances across all competitions.

However, he has started only once at club level this season after a proposed £40million switch to Everton late in the summer collapsed due to what he claimed was a late change in the contract terms.

Monaco and Everton had reportedly renegotiated the deal after Balogun - who had also been linked with Tottenham - underwent a medical and the Toffees submitted a deal sheet on Deadline Day, though it broke down from there.

Both Monaco and Balogun have confirmed publicly that the player will likely move on in January, with renewed links to a number of Premier League clubs including Pochettino’s United.

Arsenal did not insert a buy-back clause into the deal when they sold Balogun to Monaco for approximately £35m three years ago and are not thought to be interested in pursuing a potential reunion with the striker, but they did negotiate a 17.5 per cent sell-on clause that will see them bank a tidy windfall if he does indeed depart the Stade Louis II in January.

Had Balogun joined Everton for £40m in the summer as planned, around £7m of that transfer fee would have gone to Arsenal.

#1793. England: James Garner relishing midfield battle with star £200m duo

James Garner says he is loving the competition of challenging England’s two £100million midfielders for game time under Thomas Tuchel.

Garner came off the bench during Thursday’s 2-1 win over Croatia and scored what would have been his first goal for his country, but it was disallowed for a narrow offside in the build-up.

Tuchel has taken a liking to Garner, but the Everton midfielder knows he faces an almighty challenge to dislodge Declan Rice and Elliot Anderson in the middle of the park.

Rice joined Arsenal from West Ham for £105million in 2023, while Anderson was this summer signed by Manchester City from Nottingham Forest for a fee of £116m.

“I came on a little bit more advanced and had the freedom to join in with the press a little bit further up,” Garner said of his substitute appearance at Wembley against Croatia. “The main point is the freedom and just playing as you see.”

Asked whether he believes he can force his way into England’s £200m midfield, he said: “Who knows? They are very, very good players. They have been and still are, over the last few years.

“I love competition, and they are the lads in my position at the moment. But I just have to keep on going at club level.

“And when I have a chance like tonight, hopefully that goal goes in and that helps my case a little bit more. I’m just happy to be playing with such quality.”

Victory for England over Croatia set up a dramatic final Nations League group game in Madrid against world champions Spain on Sunday. The winner will finish top of the group and likely secure themselves an easier opponent for the quarter-finals in March.

Garner said of the Spain fixture: “It’s kind of like a final really. It’s a chance to test ourselves against the best in the world. It will be a good game. It’s a chance to get one back, and that’s what we’ll be looking to do.”

#1791. Mauricio Pochettino should not take Man Utd job - unless two 'needed' signings are made

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:38

Gary Neville has warned Mauricio Pochettino against becoming the next Manchester United head coach unless he is promised two new signings in January.

It was confirmed on Thursday morning that Michael Carrick has been relieved of his duties just six months after his permanent appointment, with the Red Devils revealing in a statement that they “intend to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

The man expected to replace Carrick is former Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea boss Pochettino, who reportedly has an agreement in principle to swap his current role in charge of the USA national team with the Old Trafford hotseat.

Pochettino, 54, is set to take over a Man United side languishing inside the Premier League relegation zone following the club’s worst start to a season in 40 years.

The struggling Red Devils have looked particularly vulnerable in defence, conceding 19 goals across their opening 10 league games – only Ipswich Town (20) and basement club Crystal Palace (24) having conceded more.

Ahead of Pochettino’s expected arrival, former Man United defender Neville believes that the Argentine should be assured by the club’s hierarchy that he can make at least two defensive signings in January before accepting the manager’s job.

Speaking on The Overlap, Neville said: “If I was Mauricio Pochettino now, I would be literally protecting myself up to the high heaven.

“He'll do that with a pay-off, so do that in your contract, but secondly, he needs two defenders in January, so he's got to insist that he gets two defenders in January.

“He's got to insist that he gets a minimum budget next summer for the transfer window to be able to turn this around. He's got to insist that he gets a budget that follows.

“They have to give it to him or else he shouldn't take the job.”

Neville added: “He's got to insist on the way in that there's some sort of transfer control, some form of budget there that he knows he can meaningfully change the team.

“Mauricio, I don't think is the kind of manager either who would say 'Give me half a billion' - I don't think he's that type of guy, I think he's someone who is a bit more responsible and will look at things.

"He'll want to bring players through and he'll want to develop young players - I get that and he'll do that. I just think he needs to protect himself in these next 12 months with the transfer budget. He has to.

“The only time you can insist upon it is at the very beginning and he needs two defenders in January.”

Neville, who made 602 appearances for Man United and is regarded as one of England’s greatest right-backs, did not hold back on his criticism of the Red Devils’ current defensive options.

“I mean look at the back four that he finished with on Sunday (4-4 draw with Aston Villa). It was [Diogo] Dalot left-back, [Noussair] Mazraoui right-back, Leny Yoro and Ayden Heaven,” Neville added.

“That is probably the worst back four in the Premier League. I don't know a back four that is worse than that in the Premier League right now if I watch it. I can't believe Manchester United have ended up with that back four.”

Man United have been linked with a plethora of defenders throughout this calendar year, but their top left-back target Lewis Hall signed a long-term contract extension at Newcastle in September, seemingly ending their pursuit of the Englishman.

Barcelona’s Alejandro Balde, Manchester City’s Rayan Ait-Nouri, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Rennes starlet Mahamadou Nagida are among a number of other left-backs who have been linked with Man United.

The likes of Roma’s Wesley, Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite, Fulham’s Calvin Bassey, Brentford’s Nathan Collins and Nottingham Forest’s Murillo are other defenders who are believed to be on the Red Devils’ radar ahead of the winter window.

Pochettino could be announced as Man United’s new manager before the club travels to Anfield for their next Premier League match against Liverpool on November 22.

#1790. Arsenal stars enjoy record-breaking night as Mikel Arteta handed surprise new option

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Max Dowman has become the youngest-ever player to represent England’s Under-21s on a record-breaking night for the Arsenal sensation.

Dowman, aged 16 years, 10 months and 13 days, was sent on by head coach Lee Carsley to replace ex-Gunners youngster Amario Cozier-Duberry for the final 29 minutes of Friday night’s high-profile friendly against Portugal in Bristol.

That appearance at Ashton Gate saw him break the previous record held by Jude Bellingham, who was 17 and then playing for Birmingham when he scored off the bench on his England U21 debut under Aidy Boothroyd against Kosovo in a European Championship qualifier in Pristina in September 2020.

Dowman’s maiden U21 call-up came amid a domestic suspension for his late sending off in Arsenal’s shock Carabao Cup last-16 defeat by fourth-tier Fleetwood last month, and after he was also shown a straight red card on his last appearance for England’s U19s in a friendly against the United States in September.

However, his historic cameo could not prevent the Young Lions from slipping to a second successive defeat to follow a surprise 3-1 loss to the Republic of Ireland last month that ruined their unbeaten qualifying run for next year’s Euros in the final game, with Afonso Moreira’s first-half strike sealing a 1-0 win for Portugal.

Dowman’s Arsenal team-mate Tommy Setford - currently on loan in the EFL at League One side Stevenage - will feel that he should have done better for the winning goal, but also made a string of fine saves throughout the match.

Arsenal’s Borussia Dortmund loanee Ethan Nwaneri also started the game, while England’s team featured another Gunners academy graduate in Brooke Norton-Cuffy, who now plays for Hull.

Elsewhere on an eventful Friday night for Arsenal stars away on international duty, Jurrien Timber - playing out of position at left-back - netted twice as the Netherlands thrashed Greece 7-0 to equal the record for the biggest win in Nations League history. He had never previously scored for his country in 26 caps.

Mikel Arteta will have no doubt taken note of the already versatile Timber’s excellent performance on the left-hand side of defence, which could also be an option for Arsenal in future if injuries were to befall the likes of Riccardo Calafiori, Piero Hincapie and Myles Lewis-Skelly.

Arsenal’s Christos Tzolis was on the losing side in Amsterdam and endured an evening to forget for a Greek team that took four points off Germany during the last international break and drew 2-2 with the Dutch at home, as well as winning away in Serbia.

#1789. Jesus Owono ban: Goalkeeper handed 12-match suspension after fatal collision with Jesus de Miguel

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been handed a 12-match ban following the collision that led to the tragic death of Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel.

De Miguel suffered a cardiac arrest on the pitch earlier this month during a second-division match in Spain after a heavy collision with Owono, who came racing out of his penalty area to near the halfway line to attempt to intercept a long pass forward.

Owono flew into a reckless challenge and his right knee made contact with the chest of De Miguel, earning the goalkeeper a straight red card.

De Miguel received treatment on the pitch before being taken to hospital and placed in intensive care, where he was initially reported to be stable before his condition quickly deteriorated and he died on November 3.

Under Spanish law, all deaths regarded as non-natural are subject to a judicial enquiry, with police opening an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter. However, prosecutors have said that criminal proceedings are unlikely.

Owono has now been handed a 12-match suspension from club football by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) Disciplinary Committee, which was the maximum punishment permitted under articles 102 and 52 of the RFEF ⁠Disciplinary Code.

“The assessment of the conduct under consideration in these proceedings must be based on the facts expressly recorded in the referee’s report, which states that the player was sent off for ‘violently striking an opponent in the chest with his leg, using excessive force, while the ball was in play,’” the committee said in a statement.

“The tragic outcome of the incident, resulting in the death of Jesús de Miguel, is public knowledge. In view of the nature of the conduct described and the accompanying circumstances … the maximum sanction, 12 matches of suspension, is justified.”

FC Andorra manager Carles Manso said on Thursday that Owono had yet to decide if he would return to football at all following the death of De Miguel, with the goalkeeper having said that he was dealing the “hardest days of his life” following the incident.

“These are the hardest days of my life,” he said in a statement published by his club. “I struggle to find the words, and it is very difficult for me to process anything that has happened.

“I feel immense pain over the loss of Jesús. I think of him, of his family, and of all the people who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address and I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

“But right now, honestly, I cannot think about anything other than Jesús and the pain we are going through. Rest in peace, Jesús.”

Owono plays international football for Equatorial Guinea, but is not in the squad for this month’s pair of Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers against Zimbabwe.

#1788. Rio Ferdinand claps back at fans mocking him for celebrating Man United's late equaliser against Aston Villa which left them in the relegation zone

Published: 14:15 EST, 9 November 2026 | Updated: 04:16 EST, 10 November 2026

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at football fans who criticised his reaction on social media to Manchester United's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa.

Former United defender Ferdinand drew criticism when he shared a photo of himself celebrating after the Red Devils' dramatic comeback on Sunday afternoon.

Michael Carrick's side had looked down and out at 4-2 in stoppage time, but late strikes from Joshua Zirkzee and Patrick Dorgu meant they earned a point from the game.

They did, though, remain in the relegation zone – however Ferdinand shared two snaps to his X account following full-time.

The first showed the 48-year-old with his head in his hands, and the second saw him celebrating. He captioned the post: 'From this to THIS!!! Carrick time!!!!!!!!!! Birthday weekend just got (a) tad better in the last 6 minutes…'

Fans though flooded the replies with criticism, questioning why he was 'celebrating a draw' and calling him an 'embarrassment'. Ferdinand, though, has now taken the opportunity to respond.

Rio Ferdinand has hit back at fans who criticised his response to Manchester United's draw with Aston Villa

'Let me just address something,' Ferdinand began on Rio Ferdinand Presents. 'On socials I put a picture up and little comment underneath of me going like that (celebrates).

'That's not me celebrating a point against Aston Villa, by the way, it's me celebrating a moment in a football match. It's what football does to you. It can take over your body, take over your emotions in a moment. That moment isn't the big picture.

'So all of these people saying his standards have dropped and he's celebrating a draw... I'm not celebrating a draw against Villa, I'm celebrating the moment and the fact we actually came back and showed a bit of character.

'It's always about that moment that when you calm down and you go, look where we are in the league, that's terrible, looks how things unfolded in the game, that needs work. But, in the moment, as a football fan, you are allowed to get carried away with it.

'That's what football does. If you don't know that or don't understand it or feel it, you're not a football person, so get out.'

Ferdinand hasn't shied away from criticising his former team-mate Carrick amid United's poor run of form that has left them in 18th in the Premier League table.

United came back from behind to draw 4-4 with Villa having looked down and out in the game

His assessment of Sunday's showing was more tame, with the ex-centre back describing the effort as full of both character and chaos.

He added: 'It's like we need a punch on the nose, or two or three, to start playing. But then, the flip side of it, it's character and ability plays a part in that.

'In the end, we could have won it. But they are giving us fans grey hairs. It's crazy football.'

As thrilling as Man United's fight-back may have been to some fans, manager Carrick was still forced to answer difficult questions at full-time.

Sky Sports' Patrick Davison asked the former captain what he 'expected to happen over the next few weeks' - suggesting a question mark still lingering over his tenure despite comebacks against Roma and Villa.

Carrick's response was understandably thorny, with the manager underlining that he 'probably' would not be walking away from the role.

With United chiefs Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox in the stands, Davison pushed further asking: 'What do you expect to happen? Clearly there's going to be conversation?'

This prompted Carrick to quizzically state: 'Is there?' as the pair engaged in a back-and-forth on the subject.

Eventually Carrick replied: 'You know the situation, we haven't won enough games. But I expect to move forward with things we've been working on, showing a lot of the good from today tighten up a few mistakes and win some football matches.'

United's start of one win in 10 games is still their worst since Alex Ferguson replaced Ron Atkinson 40 years ago this week.

#1787. Crystal Palace sack Pierre Sage: Club statement and update on ‘advanced talks’ with successor

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 12:40, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 14:19

Crystal Palace have announced that Pierre Sage has been relieved of his duties as head coach.

The 47-year-old has departed Selhurst Park less than five months after he was appointed the successor to Oliver Glasner, who had steered the Eagles to Conference League glory last season and a historic first FA Cup triumph the year before.

Sage arrived at Palace on the back of a successful 2025-26 campaign in charge of Lens, who finished second in Ligue 1 and won their first-ever Coupe de France trophy.

However, the Frenchman was unable to make an immediate impact in South London and has left Palace sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of his opening 10 games (W1 D2).

A 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool last weekend represented a fourth consecutive top-flight defeat for the Eagles that proved to be the final nail in the coffin for Sage, who saw his side concede a division-high 24 goals.

Palace also sit 21st in the 36-team Europa League standings with only one win from their first four games on the board thus far.

Frank de Boer (five) is the only permanent manager in Crystal Palace’s 121-year history who has overseen fewer matches than Sage (16), who departs with a 31.25% win ratio (W5 D3 L8).

Crystal Palace Football Club can confirm that Pierre Sage has left his role as Manager. The club would like to place on record its thanks to Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future. https://t.co/JcVHA6FIhe https://t.co/VAM8XnpHlq

In a club statement released on Thursday, Palace said that three members of Sage's backroom staff - Jamal Alioui, Damien Della Santa and Sandy Guichard - had also left the club.

The Eagles added: "The club thanks Pierre and his staff for their efforts during their time in South London, and wish them well for the future.

"An update on the process of appointing a new manager will be provided in due course."

It is now understood that Sage already has a new managerial job lined up, with a 'verbal agreement' said to be in place.

It was reported at the end of last month that Sean Dyche was the ‘frontrunner’ to replace Sage as Palace head coach.

The likes of Anthony Barry – Thomas Tuchel’s assistant coach at England - Vitor Pereira and Rob Edwards, Jens Berthel Askou and Ole Werner have also been linked with the Eagles job.

However, multiple reports, including one from BBC Sport, claims that Thomas Frank is now in ‘advanced talks’ to take over.

It is thought that Palace wish to finalise Frank’s appointment before their next Premier League game away against Coventry City on November 21.

Frank has been out of work since he was sacked as Tottenham Hotspur boss in February, after less than eight months in charge.

The 53-year-old, who replaced Ange Postecolgou, won only 13 of his 38 games at the helm and left the North London club languishing in 16th place in the Premier League table, five points above the relegation zone.

During a brief, trouble-filled spell in charge, Frank was unable to earn the backing of the Spurs faithful, with his tenure defined by numerous setbacks and awkward blunders including drinking from a coffee cup branded with the Arsenal badge.

However, Frank had enormous success at previous club Brentford during a memorable seven-year spell between 2018 and 2025, guiding the Bees into the Premier League and then establishing them as a competitive top-flight team, reaching a ninth-place finish in 2023.

The Dane won 132 of his 317 games in charge of Brentford and they finished as high as ninth in the Premier League under his tutelage in the 2022-23 season.

Frank stated in June that he had no intentions of taking a new job and opted to conduct media and punditry duties during the 2026 World Cup, but he now appears to be ready to jump back into management and embark on a fresh challenge with Crystal Palace.

#1785. Outstanding Leeds cut short Jaissle’s Newcastle honeymoon

The noise started in a corner of the South Stand, early in the second half. It was muffled at first, but as the ball popped from one white shirt to another, it became louder and louder, sweeping around the stadium: here was the soundtrack for a humiliation.

“Olé! Olé! Olé!” they roared and why not? Leeds were ripping Newcastle to pieces, knocking passes around them as if they were training-ground mannequins. Football has become a sport that leaves people increasingly vexed, but this was a night when – for the locals, at least – it was almost a throwback.

There was energy and ferocious tackling, a No 9 soaring like centre-forwards used to in the not-too-distant past and lots of goals as Leeds cut loose and abruptly ended whatever honeymoon Matthias Jaissle had been experiencing in charge of Newcastle.

“I suppose in football you can always find something to moan about,” Daniel Farke, the Leeds manager, said. “But this was a top-class performance.”

It has felt suspiciously like Newcastle’s start has been like an overstuffed plastic shopping bag, the handles straining to the point of snapping. Eventually they fell asunder. Leeds ran all over them and were too smart, slick and hungry, not to mention ruthless. No wonder Jaissle had nowhere to go.

The home fans were adamant this was one of the best nights Leeds have experienced under Farke and if they were prepared to say as much, you had an obligation to listen. Forget how wretched Newcastle were, Leeds had produced a performance to enable imaginations to run wild.

Centre to it all was Ao Tanaka, with his desire to keep Leeds playing forward, but it felt wrong to talk about one man when you had the unstoppable Dominic Calvert-Lewin, who would be substituted to a standing ovation, and the ubiquitous James Justin, among others.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

The foundations are being put in around the stadium for a cavernous new West Stand, and Farke’s remit is to ensure that Leeds will be firmly established in the Premier League by the time it is completed in the summer of 2028.

To be fair to Farke, he has laid a sturdy base for this team to thrive and it felt before kick-off that this was going to be a big evening for Leeds, who had made a quietly encouraging start to the campaign and had negotiated three challenging away trips without defeat.

Big? It turned out to be spectacular. The first half was so one-sided that a boxing referee would not have allowed Newcastle to come out for the second, such was the pummelling they received; wave after wave of white-shirted raids left the visitors black and blue.

Aside from one little rick inside the opening 10 minutes, when James Trafford dithered and presented Yoane Wissa with a chance to mug him, Leeds were every bit as sensational as Newcastle were shocking, seizing on the opportunity to go on a rampage.

Leeds would have been in front after 11 minutes but Ethan Ampadu’s fierce drive battered into Calvert-Lewin’s legs and bounced away. Normally in such circumstances, players will wave an arm to berate their bad luck, but Ampadu, celebrating his 26th birthday, smiled: he, like everyone else, sensed what was coming.

Jayden Bogle, Justin and Nico Elvedi all had opportunities to open the scoring earlier, but eventually, they found the weak spot. Newcastle, who had lost the influential Nico González to a potential concussion, had replaced him with Sean Steur and what an influence he would have on matters.

On the half hour, Steur was a fraction too late getting out to close down Tanaka, whose shot ricocheted off him and to Lewis Miley, before looping away from Lukas Hornicek and dropping into the corner of the net in dam-busting fashion.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Leeds were running even quicker by this point, pressing as if their lives depended on it and making tackles that were lustily acclaimed in the stands. Steur completely short-circuited in the bedlam and a ridiculous pass on the edge of his area was pounced upon by Bogle.

Out went a ball to Justin, whose cross was whipped into the penalty area, where Calvert-Lewin had climbed to get his head to it, though replays indicated his effort glanced off Bogle’s head – determining the true scorer will make for an interesting conversation.

Calvert-Lewin, at least, got the reward his efforts deserved on the cusp of half-time, spinning away from Miley and chopping inside Sven Botman before delivering the kind of finish that should make Thomas Tuchel take note when selecting his next England squad this week.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

The gloss, after those “olés”, was applied in the 59th minute when Noah Okafor put a realistic hue on the score, ramming in a finish in front of the Kop and leaving Newcastle open to the crudest mocking for the amount of money they have spent to resemble such a disorganised rabble.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Bazoumana Touré, at least, scored a consolation goal, but Jaissle barely flickered as it went in and the emotion belonged to Farke, who thundered on to the pitch at the final whistle and sought out his captain, Ampadu, who had erred in allowing Newcastle’s substitute to profit.

“That was an unnecessary goal to concede and I so wanted us to keep a clean sheet,” Farke sighed. “We deserved a clean sheet and I couldn’t help myself. I had to tell him because I am sometimes a perfectionist. We must try to stay humble, but we can be an outstanding team.”

And this, for certain, was an outstanding night.

[It was brutal out there?] That’s football. That’s the Premier League. It was clear from the start and I have said it many times. We will have ups and downs and challenges all the way. Tonight we faced that challenge. It’s tough and difficult to digest. But there is a chance to learn out of that and there’s a long time until our next match at home and that is good.

It’s clear with our young squad that there will be ups and downs and you have to bring the fundamentals on the pitch against such a physical team. Leeds are so intense, we couldn’t match that physicality. There are other aspects of course but I don’t want to make excuses. We want to learn out of it and be better.

[Were you overwhelmed as a team?] No. If you don’t bring that physicality on the pitch, you struggle.

Exactly this [message to the players]. Bring your fundamentals and we build on it. [Can you bounce back from this in your next game?] Of course. [Is your confidence hit?] No

For each manager it would be a nightmare after such a game to concede so late and not have the well-deserved clean sheet. Of course I was not happy about the situation. Doesn’t take anything away from my boys who were magnificent. Terrific start with eight points but there’s never a perfect performance. There’s always something to moan about. At very rare points [in the season] I have to criticise [for conceding].

Energy, quality, good structure, in an out of possession, which is complicated against Newcastle, In pressing them you always have to be aware of their unbelievable pace and strength in counter-attacks. We found this balance today and in the first half particularly we were dominant.

We have a good fitness level now. Need to find the right triggers to press. It’s a lot of well-structured work on the training ground. We had more chances to score tonight but overall I am very happy with our performance.

[Calvert-Lewin being praised] It is well deserved. He is in outstanding shape and plays with lots of confidence. I expect him to lead the group with some other players. His work-rate is never in doubt and to me he is one of the best strikers in the league.

The ref told me at half-time that they’ve taken it off me. I didn’t know he [Bogle] was there to be fair. I just got up and went ‘Bang!’ It is what it is. I’ll take the assist!

I didn’t know anything about it [being given credit for the second goal]. I said to the ref, I don’t fancy telling him [Calvert-Lewin]. To be fair he’s still raging. He’s raging with the goal but happy with the result.

It’s about having an understanding with the players around you. With Dom up there, you know he’s going to win everything so you have to get the runners around him.

It’s about the rotation like today. When James Justin goes wider there’s space inside. Dom occupies two centre-backs so there’s always pockets.

Regardless of the scoreline it was a tough game physically. They’re a very good side. We take it game by game, not to get carried away. Everyone’s ambitious in their own way but we have to take it game by game.

A proper stuffing for Newcastle as Leeds continue to impress and climb up to third.

James pounces on a loose ball, dribbles infield from the right. No one bothers to close him down so he eventually has a shot, blazing over with his left from 20 yards.

Late free-kick for Leeds after Livramento bundled Aaronson over. Wilson chips from the left to the far post and Muharemovic heads it back acros goal looking for a team-mate but none had made the run.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 1 (Touré) No clean sheet for Leeds. Farke is fuming after the substitute exploits an error and scores with a left-foot shot that deflects off Justin.

Livramento drives the ball 60 yards looking for Barnes but the ball skids off the turf and into Trafford’s arms.

Crunching Bard tackle on Bamba sends the ball to James who lets fly from 22 yards into the shins of a Newcastle defender.

Bard is penalised for a trip on Barnes as the game peters out.

Ampadu and Bamba collide when fighting for a loose ball but there was nothing malicious in it.

Wissa escapes a booking for a snide kick at Muharemovic’s shin.

A debatable offside call which should have been left for VAR lets Trafford off the hook when he comes out of his area to clear a ball clipped over the top. He slices it to Toure and the ref stops the game but I think Bard was playing Wissa, who found Toure, onside.

Newcastle corner on the left headed out by Elvedi and Barnes recovers the ball to start another attack with the 18-yard line stacked with players. When the diagonal comes back from left to right Barnes heads it behind for a goalkick.

Willock hooks a half-volley on to the roof of the net.

Bard → GudmundssonAaronson → OkaforWilson → Tanaka

Newcastle free-kick for a trip on Willock. Hall takes and Leeds head it out for a throw-in.

Livramento improves the quality of crosses with two that at least find the middle of the box even if they were headed away by Elvedi and Justin respectively.

Newcastle are enjoying more possession but the crossing has been awful when they do get down the flanks, Touré the latest offender.

Barnes shoots down Trafford’s throat. Barnes had thrown himself down in the box moments earlier and there was a VAR check but there was nothing like the contact required to send him swan-diving on to the grass.

Wissa gets down the right and whips over a low cross but Willock’s touch was too heavy.

There was a piece in the Athletic today saying Newcastle pivoted to Hornicek instead of pursuing Trafford again because he had a very high ceiling and was younger. He hasn’t caught much here, dropping the ball even when he chooses not to punch.

Matthias Jaissle promised high intensity, high octane, front foot football when he was interviewed for the Newcastle job. He and sporting director Ross Wilson have repeated that promise several times since he was appointed. There has been no sign of it since the opening weekend against Liverpool.

Newcastle are passive, they look disorganised in midfield and weak at the back. Oh and they barely apply pressure let alone attack dangerously.

These are early days but this performance and result had been coming. A pretty brutal reality check after all the positive noise and bold predictions in pre-season. This defeat will drop Newcastle to 12th in the table, where they finished last season under Eddie Howe.

Leeds 4 Newcastle 0 (Okafor) Ampadu hurls it into the box. A defender heads it to the edge of the area where Okafor thumps a left-footed half-volley in off the right post.

A wonderful strike with equally brilliant celebrations from Noah Okafor! 🕺 pic.twitter.com/Ce1ueKtH4x

Livramento slides in to stop Okafor’s drive down the left, giving Leeds another opportunity to throw it long.

Triple change: Livramento → DedicTouré → Fernandez-PardoWillock → Murphy

Leeds catch Newcastle playing short from the back. Stach blindsides Steur 20 yards out, tackles him, cuts inside then bends a left foot shot into the side-netting.

After Hall stings Trafford’s palms with a strike from distance. Newcastle want a penalty when the ball hits Tanaka’s arm … but it was outside the area and then Murphy, in frustration, chops down Gudmundsson and takes the booking as an occupational hazard.

Elvedi sloppily gives the ball way to Wissa who tries to set Fernandez-Pardo through down the left. Justin sticks with him and Bogle mops up after Justin was tripped.

Gudmundsson does the upended beetle when he tries to break from the corner and collides with a Newcastle player. He claims he was fouled and wthrashes about like a RL player after he’s tackled. He continues to do a Rumpelstiltskin polka of peevishness towards the ref for a while.

Newcastle corner on the left that Trafford backpedals to tip behind for another.

No changes at half-time for Newcastle as they kick off. Leeds break through the middle quickly and Calvert-Lewin seems to push the ball past Botman and shapes to shoot before Steur slides in with a crucial tackle just inside the box.

The first goal is now an own goal. The explanation is that Tanaka’s shot was on target but the deflection from Steur meant it was going wide until it hit Miley.

Now the second goal has been credited to Bogle as Calvert-Lewin’s header struck the top of his head before it went in.

You could not say that this scoreline is undeserved. Newcastle are being demolished physically. The central midfield two – Steur and Miley – just don’t have the power to screen their defence.

Leeds 3 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Leeds are running all over Newcastle who seem physically flimsy. Calvert-Lewin chops in from the left on to a flick-on, the ball takes a deflection off the Newcastle captain and he steers it into the far corner with a right-foot shot.

"They are relentless!"Dominic Calvert-Lewin caps off a dominant first-half from Leeds 💪 pic.twitter.com/S6kQykOMW9

Calvert-Lewin is booked for catching Botman in the face with a straight arm rather than a swinging arm. ‘Reckless but not violent.’ Trafford had punchd the corner away at the back post to set Leeds off on a counter.

Tanaka gives the ball away carelessly in midfield and Newcastle work it to Wissa who chops inside past Elvedi, hangs out his own leg looking for contact and hits the deck. The ref waves play on and the ball runs to Barnes in the left of the area. He shapes to shoot but Muharemovic sprinted over to make a fine block-tackle, forcing it behind for a corner.

Newcastle are rocking here. They cannot win a tackle.

For those of us who have watched all Newcastle United’s games this season, this was coming. They do not have any consistent attacking threat, they do no create chances and they are not secure at the back either.

They’ve survived by converting the very few chances they create in games but they have not even had a shot in the first half here.

Leeds should be three up after Hornicek fumbled Gudmundsson’s shot from the left. The ball falls to Calvert-Lewin five yards out and he triesto dink it over the keeper who recovers well to smother it.

Leeds 2 Newcastle 0 (Calvert-Lewin) Newcastle try to play the ball out from the back, give it away cheaply to Bogle who feeds Justin haring down the right. He is ostensibly the right centre-back but he is a full-back by trade and stands up a perfect near-post cross that Calvert-Lewin hangs in the air to bury with the firmest of headers. In fact it transpires that his downward header struck Bogle and another deflection benefits rampant Leeds –162 seconds between the goals.

"He just cannot stop scoring at Elland Road" 🔥Dominic Calvert-Lewin makes it 2-0 to Leeds! pic.twitter.com/Pv1TEpc5Qj

Leeds 1 Newcastle 0 (Tanaka) Good move, spawny finish. Tanaka sprays a pass out to Okafor who drives at Dedic then picks out Tanaka who had held his run. He cushions the pass then lets fly. The ball hits Steur, deflects on to Miley and then loops into the right of the goal with Hornicek understandably stranded.

Ao Tanaka's deflected effort puts Leeds ahead! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/cYXVi3LOAO

Good tackle by Steur on Bogle stops the Leeds right-back flying forward after Calvert-Lewin’s flick-on.

Newcastle really are not afraid to launch the ball forward are they? Football tactics are constantly evolving and fashions come back around. What better way to play through a press than to bypass the midfield completely? The hope is it will also cause the centre-backs problems, get them facing their own goal under pressure from one of Newcastle’s rapid forward players in a foot race.

It almost worked a couple of times in the first half but it should be pointed out that the best direct/long ball teams of the past tended to have a striker who was dominant in the air. Newcastle do not currently have one which does limit their threat from flick ons.

Newcastle break from defending a long throw. Wissa carries it 60 yards but with Murphy and Fernadez-Pardo better placed, he tries to shoot from 25 yards and plinks it straight at Trafford, provoking an inevitable ‘Woooooooo’.

From the resulting long throw Elvedi is found at the back post, unmarked and attempts to volley it towards goal, missing the ball entirely. It was so wild that even the Leeds staff laugh at how inept it was.

Leeds have a corner when they use one of their signature moves, Bogle cutting in from the right across the back four to take a ball over the top. He controls it but cannot force it past Thiaw.

Hornicek claws out the corner to Bogle 18 yards out. He puts his laces through a volley that Hornicek parries up high and punches away when he has a second go.

Newcastle chip it long again, this time down the right. Gudmundsson holds off Murphy and Leeds will have the relief of a goal-kick.

Leeds are finding it hard now to play through Newcastle’s high press and the intensity with which they are hounding keeper and defenders.

Newcastle keep looking to use their pace with balls over the top for Wissa, Murphy and Fernandez-Pardo. Wissa closes Trafford down quickly again. He needs to release it with more urgency.

Gonzalez hs not recovered from being struck on the head by the ball and is being replaced by Steur as a concussion sub.

Justin heads over his own bar when Newcastle chip a long pass down the inside right. Wissa beats Muharemovic and tries to find Fernandez-Pardo but Justin got there first. Newcastle go short from the corner and Leeds force them back into their own half.

Terrific save from Hornicek down low to his right. Tanaka’s cross from the left found Justin creeping round the back on the right and heading across goal from the back post. Bogle swivelled and tried a sidewinder flick that was arrowing towards the bottom left corner until the keeper swooped to turn it away with his right hand.

Wissa is ticking, feeling he is getting nothing from the referee when challenging for the ball, the latest incident involving a collision with Justin which was 50-50.

Leeds have been the slicker of the two sides, their passing and movement causing the full-backs problems. Okafor dribbles down the left and centres. Stach lays it back to Ampadu who hammers a half-volley from 18 yards that poleaxes Calvert-Lewin who was in an offside position.

Newcastle fans sing ‘There’s only one Kevin Keegan’ as the visitors’ defence sweeps the ball around. When they knock the ball up the inisde-right channel Wissa is penalised for swinging his arm and catching Muharemovic in the mooey.

Wissa presses Trafford high and the goalkeeper is a bit too casual but gets away with it. His clearance bounces off the attacker’s shin and loops out to the right. Leeds shift it quickly out to the left with Gudmundsson and Okafor bombing forward. A vicious cross from the left-back hits a Newcastle leg, loops up and smaxks Gonzales flush in the face, knocking him off his feet. The ref stops play.

Two bad moments for Newcastle early on. Lewis Hall caught out by a simple run and pass behind him and then, from the resulting corner Mathias Fernandez-Pardo looked very fortunate, in my opinion, to avoid conceding a penalty for handball.

He got the benefit of the doubt presumably because the ball bounced up onto his hand as he tried to bring it under control and he did not intend to control it with his hand or knock it away. The handball law confuses me but there is a higher threshold now.

Stach tackles Wissa in the centre-circle. Wissa is playing behind Fernandez-Pardo. Ampadu receives a long pass over the top, coming back from an offside position in the nick of time.

Fernandez-Pardo’s outstretched left arm is struck in the penalty area with the ball after they win the header but the ref waves play on and stops the game for a foul on the new striker.

It’s never a problem to come to Elland Road and the singing of Marching On Together before kick-off makes this one of the top three atmospheres in the country, easily. There are problems with VAR, though, and the whole stadium has just seen the ball strike Matias Fernanzes-Pardo’s hand in the area. The reason it is a problem is because we have become conditioned to thinking every time a ball touches someone on the arm in the area, a penalty should be awarded. It is preposterous that faceless beaks have distorted the game so much.

Leeds kick off, attacking the South Stand, from left to right, as they always prefer to do. Justin and Bogle combine on the right and Bogle bends a pass inside HAll to Stach who chooses to cross rather than shoot. It hits Botman and goes out for a corner.

Leeds are in their home kit of white with yellow and blue pinstripe hoops, Newcastle in their navy away kit.

Anthony [Elanga] is injured. Unfortunately we have to investigate further how long he will be out but obviously we miss him. We wish him to come back as quickly as possible. It could be [a long-term injury] but he will get another MRI next week and then we’ll see.

Lewis Hall is the perfect player profile for how we play. he is a young lad still and we are very excited [that he has signed a new contract].

The start was not easy. We didn’t have lots of time to prepare for pre-season and that’s one reason we are happy and satisfied with the start. But there is potential and we will work hard on the margins we want to improve.

There will be a lot of excitement surrounding Mathias Fernandez-Pardo’s first start for Newcastle United following his deadline day move from Lille but also keep an eye on Jacob Murphy on the right wing.

Fernandez-Pardo starts with a clean slate at Newcastle, Murphy has a lot of baggage and he has been a popular online target for criticism over the last year or so.

Indeed, some sections of the fanbase were stunned Newcastle rejected a £15m offer from Nottingham Forest on deadline day for a player who has entered the final 12 months of his contract.

Murphy has his limitations, sure and he can be infuriating sometimes when he gives the ball away cheaply, but there is a reason Matthias Jaissle was adamant he could not be sold.

Part of that is due to the fact he does not have another specialist right winger behind Anthony Elanga who misses the Leeds game through injury.

But Murphy is also valued for his experience and his training ground presence. He has been at the club a long time, working under Rafa Benítez, Steve Bruce and Eddie Howe and is a boyhood Newcastle fan.

Jaissle was not willing to lose that from his dressing room. Ultimately, though, Murphy has to perform on the pitch to justify the faith shown in him.

There are not many other options to fill that position while Elanga is missing. Harvey Barnes does not like playing on the right, Amar Dedic is a full back and so is Tino Livramento.

This is an opportunity for Murphy to silence his detractors and prove the faith Jaissle has put in him is not misplaced. At the age of 31, he knows he is not the most popular or appreciated player at the club but he has never shirked or complained about that.

He formed a potent partnership with Alexander Isak when he was leading the line for Newcastle. Can he do the same with the new boy Fernandez-Pardo?

Mind you I remember his visit to Elland Road in 1982-83. Not for the faint hearted. In fact it was a disgrace when he was hit by a coin. And yet he was always gracious about Leeds and particularly fond of Don Revie. He was one of very few football people without a strong Leeds United connection who went to his funeral in 1989.

Apparently he was injured in training, the nature of the injury is unspecified.

Newcastle have made a very good start particularly in their transitional moments on the counter-attack. We have to be switched on today to get the next points.

After many years of suffering our supporters deserve it [high expectations]. It’s good but we are far away from not being humble. Our feet are on the ground. We know the second year is always difficult. We have made a good start and it is always important to ride the momentum as long as possible.

Eddie Howe has left a legacy and the culture he created is still around. Matthias has to work with it. They are unbeaten. they are very dangerous with many pacy players up front. It’s important not to lose the ball too easily and always be switched on against Newcastle.

Leeds United Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle, Ampadu, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; Stach, Okafor; Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes Zetterer, Bard, Bijol, Longstaff, Aaronson, Wilson, James, Bahoya, Nmecha.

Newcastle United (4-2-3-1) Hornicek; Dedic, Thiaw, Botman, Hall; González, L Miley; Murphy, Fernandez-Pardo, Barnes; Wissa. Substitutes Pope, Livramento, Schär, Bamba, Steur, Touré, Willock, Ramsey, M Miley.

Good evening and welcome to live coverage of Leeds United vs Newcastle United, the last Premier League match of the fourth round of fixtures for the 2026-27 season. Both clubs have made unbeaten starts with one win and two draws each and a win today for wither would send them up to fourth. The two sides met at Elland Road in the third match of last season which ended in a 0-0 draw but the return fixture at St James’ Park was one of the games of the season, a ding-dong match that Leeds led 0-1, 1-2 and 2-3, the latter until the 91st minute and yet still lost 4-3.

The architect of that victory for Newcastle was the Leeds’ fans’ incubus, a player commonly known around Elland Road as ‘Harvey F------- Barnes’. His two goals that night were his sixth and seventh against Leeds in eight matches for Leicester and the Toon. Back in the last century and at the turn of this one, Alan Shearer scored 21 league goals in 23 games against Leeds for Blackburn Rovers and Newcastle, it can feel like one bogeyman passing the baton to another.

Newcastle’s sound form with their new model team this season has been based on searing pace and their ability on the counter whether with runners, in the case of Anthony Elanga, or with long diagonals against Tottenham that ripped a hole in the left side of their defence. Leeds rallied from being overrun by Brentford at half-time in their last home game to switch from three at the back to four and wrest back the initiative and while they reverted for the Brighton draw, in both games it was the introduction of Ao Tanaka in midfield that gave them control.

It is genuinely hard to decide whether the 6-3 defeat by Chelsea in the Carabao Cup from being 2-0 up at Stamford Bridge is significant to Leeds league form. One simplistic way of looking at it would be to say Leeds reserves were better than Chelsea’s reserves in the first half and Chelsea’s first-team were better than Leeds reserves and their shaky, debutant keeper in the second. But any similar defensive frailties tonight and there will be jitters over the next week before the international break. Newcastle, by contrast, toiled in their 1-0 victory over Millwall but the result glosses over a lack of incision for long spells of it.

Joe Rodon is out for Leeds for at least another month while Newcastle have changed to withholding information about their treatment room under Matthias Jaissle who says that it should be ‘confidential’. We do know that Joelinton, William Osula and Dan Burn are likely to still be out given the nature of their injuries but Amar Dedic, who came off at half-time at the New Den with a thigh or hamstring problem, may be back.

#1784. Manchester clubs to race for Malo Gusto

According to talkSPORT, both Manchester United and Manchester City are monitoring the situation of Malo Gusto as uncertainty grows over the defender’s future at Chelsea. The French right-back has seen his role reduced since the arrival of Xabi Alonso at Stamford Bridge and is increasingly being linked with a move away from west London.

Gusto has not started a Premier League match since September and has fallen behind Josh Acheampong in the battle for the right-back position, despite club captain Reece James spending time on the sidelines through injury.

Both Manchester clubs are understood to be interested in the 23-year-old, although it remains unclear whether either side will submit a formal offer during the January transfer window. However, any move from City could be complicated due to the club’s ongoing legal and regulatory situation, with the outcome of their appeal still pending.

Manchester City were previously linked with a move for Gusto and had considered a reunion with former Chelsea manager Enzo Maresca.

Chelsea value the defender at around £75 million.

Manchester United’s pursuit could also be influenced by changes at Old Trafford. With Mauricio Pochettino confirmed as the successor to Michael Carrick, the club’s transfer priorities may be reassessed once the new manager fully evaluates his squad.

Liverpool reportedly tried to sign Gusto on loan at the very end of the summer transfer window, but Chelsea were not interested in sanctioning a temporary move.

#1783. Expected Points and clinical shooting: Stats highlight worries about sustainability of Milan’s Serie A form

AC Milan have collected more points than they deserved so far in the 2026-27 Serie A season, according to statistical data.

As MilanPress write, the Expected Points ranking makes for worrying reading. The metric compares the points actually earned by Serie A teams with those expected based on performances and chances created and conceded in the first 11 rounds of the league season.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The Rossoneri have earned 24 points compared to approximately 17 expected, meaning they are ‘over-performing’ by seven points. Milan are currently fourth in the table behind Lazio, Inter and Roma, but they should be a few places lower.

Inter are second with 28 actual points, but should have collected around 26, while Juventus are on 18 points earned versus the expected 21. Napoli also obtained less than the data indicated they should have, with 15 actual points compared to the approximately 19 expected.

The numbers, therefore, reveal a Milan that is particularly effective in turning its performances into tangible results. This is a positive aspect in terms of the league table, but also food for thought. Is it sustainable moving forwards?

Another interesting statistic has come from Kickest, which perhaps highlights why Ruben Amorim’s side have been able to out-perform what the data suggests.

They reveal that there are 113 players with at least 10 shots in Serie A so far in 2026-27. The top four with the best conversion rates have something in common: they play for the Diavolo.

➤ Rabiot — 41.7% (5 goals) ➤ Moreira — 40.0% (4) ➤ Cisse — 38.5% (5) ➤ Pulisic — 36.4% (4) ➤ De Bruyne — 30.0% (3)

It is reminiscent of something we published in January, when the shooting numbers under Massimiliano Allegri were similarly remarkable. As we know, a late-season collapse ended up coming.

Then there was the revelation from Sky after the Genoa game, as they looked at data per 30 minutes of possession. Milan are first in Serie A for build-up actions, but they are 20th for entries into the final third and entries into the opposition box.

Amorim’s side are 19th for percentage of touches in the attacking third and 18th in percentage of touches in the opposition box. So, Milan must get much better at generating and sustaining pressure, or the results might start to regress.

Welcome to our Live Comments section, where new comments will appear automatically

All I learned from this stat is that Milan is lucky. We have no presence in opposition box and bailed out by lucky shooting? Kind of makes sense considering Maignan saved us in two back to back games too.

It’s not luck. It’s quality of the players. But the issue is that we create far too few chances. If we could create as much as other clubs in the top-5 we’d probably be 2nd right now because our players are great at actually converting the chances.

You can get lucky 15 times in a season. But you won’t get lucky 50 times. Check last season.

If you constantly let opponents have a lot of chances games like Bologna will happen more, not less. So, they are playing like sh*t, but some people can’t see that as they need 3 loses in a row for their brain cells to activate.

Stats are in general weapons utilized to push agendas. Give me whatever random figures you wish and tell me if I need to explain good or bad performance and I will cook the data to support your argument.

There’s definitely points lost because of the coach, usually for his starting 11 choice and it’s not a matter of squad depth only.

Still, even our bad games are easier to swallow than most of last year’s good games.

😂😂😂😂 Stats are statistic of the game, nothing else.

#1782. How Pep Guardiola feels about USA job after Mauricio Pochettino to Man Utd manager update

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 13:22

The USA national team would like to appoint Pep Guardiola as their new manager to succeed Manchester United-bound Mauricio Pochettino, according to a report.

The Red Devils officially confirmed the sacking of head coach Michael Carrick on Thursday and it is understood that an agreement in principle has been reached for Pochettino to take the reins at Old Trafford.

Man United are said to have made contact with the USA and are willing to pay the £7.4m release clause in Pochettino’s contract, though the Red Devils would be comfortable with him taking charge of international matches against Haiti on Saturday and Wednesday.

USA would have ideally liked to have retained the services of Pochettino, who was appointed head coach in September 2024 and oversaw the country’s 2026 World Cup campaign before signing a contract extension in August to keep him in charge until the summer of 2030.

However, The Athletic reports that former Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City boss Guardiola is expected to become a ‘top target’ for the USA national team in the event that Pochettino moves to Man United.

Their pursuit of Guardiola would not be straightforward, though, as the Catalan has shown little interest in an imminent return to management since ending his legendary 10-year career at the Etihad Stadium in the summer.

Guardiola turned down the opportunity to become Italy head coach earlier this year, with the president of the Italian Football Federation (FIGC), Giovanni Malago, telling La Repubblica: “Pep was honest. He took a sabbatical, partly for family reasons, but if he’d done anything, he would have done it with us.”

Nevertheless, Guardiola is said to have previously had dialogue with USA, and has long been intrigued by the possibility of working in America.

Guardiola was allegedly contacted by USA, along with Jurgen Klopp, before they ended up hiring Pochettino to replace Gregg Berhalter in 2024.

Speaking about USA after Pochettino was appointed, Guardiola told reporters: "The USA is fascinating to try to build a project for many years and be able to get the national team to the next step.

“The potential with the USA is there, given the number of people and sports, and so on.

"I wish [Pochettino] and the USA - I have friends there - the best of luck. I know he's a top-class manager, an experienced manager."

Following his 2012 departure from Barcelona, Guardiola spent a year-long sabbatical in New York City, living with his family in a luxury apartment near Central Park where he enjoyed a rare sense of anonymity.

After a decade in charge of Man City – where he won 20 trophies including six Premier League titles – Guardiola has since become a Global Ambassador for the club and stated how he plans to take an extended break from management.

"After my contract with City, I'm going to stop. I'm sure," he said in May 2025. "I don't know if I'm going to retire, but I'm going to take a break. How I want to be remembered, I don't know."

In a separate interview, he added: "So I'm not retiring, but I will take a break, for sure. When I finish here, I will take a break. I need to make a stop, that's all.”

As well as the USA, Guardiola has been tipped to manage England at some stage in the future, though Thomas Tuchel is currently in charge of the Three Lions and is expected to stay at least until the end of the 2028 European Championship.

#1781. MK Dons vs Burton Albion - prediction, team news, lineups

By Matthew Cooper | 12 Nov 2026 13:29, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 13:29

MK Dons will be looking to continue their good form when they welcome Burton Albion to Stadium MK on Saturday afternoon.

The hosts currently sit 12th in the League One table, while the visitors are 15th.

MK Dons have picked up 18 points from 13 matches so far, but their recent form has been excellent, with five consecutive victories across all competitions.

In their last league game the Dons thumped Doncaster Rovers 6-1, with Aaron Collins scoring four goals, and they followed that up with a 2-1 FA Cup victory over Swindon Town.

Paul Warne's side then beat Bromley 2-1 in the EFL Trophy on Tuesday, with Callum Paterson and Jack Burke finding the net.

The Dons will be full of confidence heading into Saturday's game and it is worth noting that they have scored 26 goals in their last seven home matches across all competitions.

Burton, meanwhile, have picked up 17 points from 14 matches and would leapfrog MK Dons with a victory on Saturday.

Gary Bowyer's side have only picked up one victory in their last six league games, but they did enjoy an impressive 4-0 FA Cup win over Rushden & Diamonds last weekend.

Mark O'Mahony, Raphael Borges Rodrigues, Charlie Webster and Zac Scutt were on target for Burton and they will take confidence from that result, although a much-changed side was beaten 3-0 by Notts County in the EFL Trophy three days later.

The Brewers also have a poor recent record against MK Dons, having not beaten them in their last seven meetings across all competitions.

MK Dons will be without in-form striker Collins, who has been called up by Wales, and Paterson is expected to partner Sam Nombe up front as a result.

Alex Gilbey, Ryan Wintle and Dan Crowley are set to continue in midfield.

Burton are missing Toby Sibbick and Gbemi Arubi due to international commitments.

O'Mahony is expected to lead the line, with support from Webster and Will Collar.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

His goal in Genoa seemed easy because he made it so, but it wasn’t. Adrien Rabiot’s pass was quite slow, the distance to the goal wasn’t that close, Genoa were exposed after losing the ball but Bijlow wasn’t in a particularly bad position, and beating him required precision.

Other strikers in those circumstances may have opted for a powerful finish. Not Cisse. He looked for the corner and found it with a lovely precise strike, one which revealed everything about the groove he has found himself in.

#1779. Man Utd managers since Ferguson: Every manager's record, win percentage and time in charge

By Calum Burrowes | 12 Nov 2026 13:48, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 15:21

Manchester United are expected to confirm Mauricio Pochettino as their new head coach following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, who has been relieved of his duties at Old Trafford.

The former Southampton and Tottenham Hotspur boss is expected to leave his role with the United States to take charge of the 20-time English champions, with another managerial change set to begin a new chapter at the club.

Since Alex Ferguson's retirement in 2013, United have appointed a succession of permanent managers and interim coaches, with varying degrees of success.

Here, Sports Mole looks at every manager to take charge of the Red Devils since Ferguson's departure, examining their time in charge, overall record and win percentage.

David Moyes was selected to succeed Ferguson in July 2013 after impressing during his time at Everton, but his spell at Old Trafford proved considerably more difficult than anticipated.

The Scot won the Community Shield in his first competitive fixture, beating Championship side Wigan Athletic 2-0, but United struggled for consistency throughout the season.

Moyes was dismissed in April 2014 after the club's hopes of qualifying for the Champions League had faded, with United eventually finishing seventh in the Premier League.

Now 63, the Scottish manager is back at Everton for a second spell on Merseyside, having returned to the club in January 2025.

Record: 51 matches, 27 wins, 9 draws, 15 defeats

Following Moyes's departure, former United midfielder Ryan Giggs took temporary charge for the final four matches of the 2013-14 season.

Giggs won two, drew one and lost one of those fixtures, including a 4-0 victory over Norwich City.

His brief spell gave him a 50% win percentage, but he was not retained as the club's permanent manager.

Record: 4 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 1 defeat

Louis van Gaal arrived in the summer of 2014 after guiding the Netherlands to the World Cup semi-finals in Brazil, bringing considerable managerial experience to Old Trafford.

The Dutchman won 54 of his 103 matches in charge and secured the FA Cup in his second season, beating Crystal Palace in the final.

However, United's failure to qualify for the Champions League proved costly, and Van Gaal was dismissed in May 2016, just two days after lifting the trophy.

Record: 103 matches, 54 wins, 25 draws, 24 defeats

"The Special One" became United's third permanent manager since Ferguson in May 2016, going on to record the highest win percentage of any permanent appointment since the legendary Scot's departure, with 84 victories from 144 matches at a rate of 58.3%.

The Portuguese enjoyed a successful first season, winning the Community Shield, League Cup and Europa League, before guiding the Red Devils to second place in the Premier League in 2017-18.

However, results and performances deteriorated during his third campaign, and he was dismissed in December 2018.

Record: 144 matches, 84 wins, 32 draws, 28 defeats

Former United striker Ole Gunnar Solskjaer initially arrived as caretaker boss in December 2018, enjoying an impressive run of results before being handed the job permanently.

Across 168 matches, Solskjaer recorded 91 wins, 37 draws and 40 defeats, giving him a win percentage of 54.2% and cementing his status as one of the most popular managers among United fans since Ferguson's departure.

United reached the Europa League final  in 2021 and finished second in the Premier League that season, but a poor run of form during the following campaign led to his departure in November 2021.

Record: 168 matches, 91 wins, 37 draws, 40 defeats

Carrick took temporary charge following the Norwegian's dismissal, overseeing three matches between November and December 2022.

The former Tottenham and England midfielder won two and drew one, leaving him unbeaten during his first brief spell and with a win rate of 66.7%.

He subsequently left the club's coaching staff following the appointment of Ralf Rangnick and went on to manage Middlesbrough before returning to Old Trafford earlier this year.

Record: 3 matches, 2 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Ralf Rangnick was appointed interim manager in December 2021 and was expected to oversee a transition before moving into a consultancy role at the end of the season.

However, his time in charge proved difficult, with United winning just 11 of their 29 matches, drawing 10 and losing eight.

His 37.9% win percentage was the lowest of any manager to take charge of the club since Ferguson at that point.

Ralf Rangnick has since spent over four years in charge of Austria, guiding the national team to the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

Record: 29 matches, 11 wins, 10 draws, 8 defeats

Erik ten Hag arrived in May 2022 and made an encouraging start to life in Manchester, winning the League Cup in his first season and restoring the Red Devils to the Champions League.

The Dutchman recorded 70 victories in 128 matches, giving him a win percentage of 54.7%, and added the FA Cup to his trophy collection in 2024.

Nevertheless, inconsistent league performances and a poor start to the 2024-25 campaign resulted in his dismissal in October 2024.

Record: 128 matches, 70 wins, 23 draws, 35 defeats

Van Nistelrooy stepped in as caretaker boss following Ten Hag's departure, having previously served as part of the Dutchman's coaching staff.

The former United striker made an immediate impression, winning three and drawing one of his four matches in charge.

His 75% win percentage is the highest on the list, although his spell was considerably shorter than those of the club's permanent appointments.

Since leaving the Red Devils, Van Nistelrooy has gone on to manage Leicester City, but was dismissed after winning just five of his 27 matches in charge of the Foxes.

Record: 4 matches, 3 wins, 1 draw, 0 defeats

Amorim was appointed in November 2024 after impressing at Sporting Lisbon, but his time at Old Trafford proved challenging despite arriving with a strong reputation.

The Portuguese won 24 of his 63 matches, recording a win rate of 38.1%, and struggled to establish consistency during his time in charge.

His spell ended in January 2026, with United having failed to make the progress expected.

Record: 63 matches, 24 wins, 18 draws, 21 defeats

Former United midfielder Darren Fletcher was placed in temporary charge following Amorim's departure in January 2026.

Fletcher oversaw two matches, drawing one and losing the other, before the club turned to Carrick.

His short spell therefore ended without a victory.

Carrick returned to Old Trafford in January 2026, initially taking charge until the end of the season after United dismissed Amorim, who is currently in charge of AC Milan.

His second spell began impressively, with 12 wins from his first 17 matches helping the Red Devils secure a third-place finish in the Premier League and a return to Champions League football.

Carrick subsequently signed a new contract in May, but his fortunes changed dramatically during the 2026-27 campaign.

United struggled for consistency and found themselves in the relegation zone after 10 league matches, with their dramatic 4-4 draw against Aston Villa proving to be Carrick's final fixture.

The club confirmed his departure on November 12, bringing his second spell to an end less than six months after he signed a new deal with the club, leaving United 18th in the league.

Record: 32 matches, 15 wins, 8 draws, 9 defeats

#1778. Leaving USA for Man Utd ‘one of the most difficult decisions of my career’, says Pochettino

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

A teary Mauricio Pochettino said leaving the United States national team to join Manchester United was "one of the most difficult decisions of my career".

Pochettino was announced as United's new head coach on Friday, though he will take charge of the USA's two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final against Haiti before making the move to Manchester.

It marks a return to the Premier League for Pochettino, who has previously managed Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

He took over as the USA's head coach in September 2024, leading them to the Gold Cup final in 2025, though they lost to Mexico in the showpiece.

However, the USA only managed a run to the last 16 at the World Cup. While it was their joint-best finish at the tournament since reaching the last eight in 2002, more was arguably expected of the co-hosts.

Pochettino, who had signed a new four-year contract with the USA following the World Cup, acknowledged that it was not an easy decision for him to leave his role.

"In some part, this is a very sad decision," an emotional Pochettino said in his press conference ahead of the first leg against Haiti.

"In another part, we are professionals. This is the next step to try and make your dreams come true.

"The most important thing is that we leave here, the moments we shared together, the things that we accomplished… all the standards we put together, we have increased.

"I haven't prepared that speech! It all came from the heart. Thank you for giving me the capacity to dream big. The players want to put the country and federation in the place they want to be.

"The human being is everything. That is why this is a difficult decision. A big thank you from my heart. We learnt a lot from this country, these amazing people.

"One of the most difficult decisions of my career."

Mauricio Pochettino has agreed to become the Manchester United men’s head coach.

— Manchester United (@ManUtd) November 13, 2026

Of managers to oversee 30+ Premier League games, Pochettino (51%) has the 19th-best win ratio in the competition's history, winning 150 games.

Pochettino has been linked with the United job in the past, and was seemingly close to joining the club in 2022 before they appointed Erik ten Hag.

And he acknowledged a move to United was not one he could turn down.

When asked about leaving for United just three months after his new USA deal, Pochettino said: "It's obvious. I never said I wanted to go back, but they know there aren't too many opportunities that happen in your career like Manchester United. When it arrives, it's difficult to turn down.

"When we decided together to extend our commitment, it was a commitment for the federation, just in case. We were very committed. It was to help the federation, just in case that didn't work for four years.

"When things start to become big and big, players are very sensitive, but the stuff is too. All was so quick because we arrived here last Friday, and [on] Sunday afternoon, this type of situation [talks with United] started to appear.

"We were talking with the federation, and [Thursday], when the agreement was reached, we had a meeting, and I communicated with the players.

"They were very supportive. US Soccer and Manchester United agreed we would continue, and that will not change our commitment.

"The situation is not ideal. But in life, football moves quickly. We need to move forward to keep that relationship and the memories we shared."

Pochettino insists his full focus remains on leading the USA through his final two matches.

The first leg against Haiti takes place on Saturday, before Pochettino's final game comes in the return leg three days later.

His first game in charge of Man Utd will come against Liverpool on November 22.

By LUKE AUGUSTUS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR

Published: 03:12 EST, 10 November 2026 | Updated: 05:18 EST, 10 November 2026

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookies' leading candidate to replace under-fire Michael Carrick as Manchester United head coach should the latter get sacked.

As reported by Daily Mail Sport late on Monday night, Carrick is facing the sack during this November international break as a result of United's disastrous season so far.

Scrutiny on his role has intensified with the Red Devils now in the relegation zone despite salvaging a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino is currently in charge of the US national team, but his contract includes a £7million release clause. However, it is yet to be determined the true value of prising Pochettino out as that figure doesn't include buying out his backroom staff.

It is also believed within Pochettino's deal that there is another clause which would allow him to leave his US role for particular high-profile jobs, such as at Old Trafford.

Mauricio Pochettino is the bookmakers' favourite to become the next Man United head coach

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is expected to get the sack after a poor start

#1775. Pierre Sage already has new job ‘agreed’ after Crystal Palace sacking confirmed

By Oliver Thomas | 12 Nov 2026 14:07

Pierre Sage has officially been sacked by Crystal Palace, but he already has a new job lined up according to reports.

The 47-year-old arrived at Selhurst Park with big boots to fill after his predecessor Oliver Glasner won the 2025 FA Cup and Conference League last season.

Sage signed a three-year contract with the Eagles in June and has now departed his role in South London less than five months later following a disappointing start to the campaign.

The Frenchman has left Palace sitting rock bottom of the Premier League table after losing seven of his opening 10 top-flight matches (W1 D2), with his team conceding a division-high 24 goals.

Palace also find themselves languishing in 21st position in the 36-team Europa League standings with only one win from their first four matches so far.

Sage’s sacking was confirmed on Thursday, four days after the Eagles suffered a 3-1 home defeat to Liverpool in the Premier League.

While many managers may prefer a period of time away from football to recharge their batteries and assess their options, it appears that Sage is ready to jump straight back in to management in familiar surroundings.

According to Foot Mercato journalists Sebastien Denis and Santi Aouna, Sage has a ‘verbal agreement’ in place to return to Lens, where he left in the summer to join Palace.

Lens are on the lookout for a new head coach after parting ways with Yannick Cahuzac, who lost six of his nine games during a brief 56-day spell in charge which concluded with a humiliating 9-1 Champions League home defeat to Como.

Le Sang et Or have, in fact, had two managers since Sage left in the summer, as Cahuzac had taken over from Dino Toppmoller who was sacked after just 91 days at the helm following disagreements around structural changes at the club.

It is understood that Lens chiefs have set a ‘very clear deadline’ for Sage to be re-appointed within the next 72 hours, giving him time to prepare for their next Ligue 1 match against Toulouse on November 21.

Sage would allegedly return to Lens on a 'very decent salary' within the limits set by the Lens hierarchy.

A return to Lens for Sage would seemingly be warmly welcomed by the club’s supporters who enjoyed a memorable 2025-26 campaign under his leadership.

Sage was named Ligue 1 Manager of the Year last season after steering Lens to an impressive second-placed finish behind champions Paris Saint-Germain, qualifying for the Champions League.

The former Lyon boss also guided Lens to their first-ever Coupe de France triumph in their 120-year history, and departed after only one season in charge with a respectable 67.5% win rate.

Lens currently sit down in 11th place in the Ligue 1 table, five points above the relegation zone and seven points adrift of the top three after 10 matches.

In the Champions League, Le Sang et Or occupy 33rd position in the 36-team League Phase standings after losing three of their opening four matches, but they still have a chance of securing at least a knockout round playoff place.
