#1729. Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Home » Home 2 » Liverpool vs Arsenal Preview: Team News, Tactics, Lineups and Prediction

Table-toppers Arsenal travel to Anfield tonight with their first Premier League trophy since the ‘invincibles’ season of 2004 in sight. The Gunners top the table and with stuttering performances from Manchester City and a Leicester City whose fairytale run seems at an end, and are in pole position to finish the current campaign as champions.

While Jurgen Klopp’s men are still finding their way inconsistently since his appointment, Arsenal are in top form with five victories out of their last six matches. In comparison, Liverpool have been as easy to predict as a magic 8 ball, with impressive wins over Leicester City and Manchester City, but accompanied with horrific losses against Watford and West Ham. With fourth place still within grasp and with an impressive record against the table topping teams this season, Liverpool would look to give their long suffering fans some cheer with which to greet this New Year.

The Reds desperately need a victory to steady the ship as their erratic and wayward form sees them enter 2016 still outside the top 4 and distant from any title challenge.

With a host of injuries to his main XI, Jurgen Klopp could be forgiven for dipping into the transfer market so early. The Reds have captured QPR right-back Steven Caulker along with Marko Grujic in the January transfer window.

With Grujic returning to his former club Red Star Belgrade on loan, Steven Caulker is likely to be given a run out as a substitute with the current spate of Liverpool injuries.

Ings, Sturridge, Lovren, Coutinho, Origi and Flanagan are amongst the Liverpool afflicted and will take no part in the match ahead. With Lovren out, Kolo Toure and Mamadou Sakho look likely to be Klopp’s first choice central defending partnership.

Alberto Moreno and Nathaniel Clyne should start as full-backs for the Liverpool side and will be crucial in any attempt to penetrate the Gunner’s defences. Emre Can and Lucas should marshal the midfield, while James Milner, Firmino and Adam Lallana look to give Petr Cech some concerns about his goal. Leading the line should be Christian Benteke, who’s lack of form doesn’t threaten this match as manager Klopp has few options in his position.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Mignolet; Clyne, Sakho, Toure, Moreno; Lucas, Can, Firmino, Lallana, Milner, Benteke.

Arsenal must show that they have the one quality required of all champions : Consistency. The task is hereby straightforward for Wenger’s men. Win, keep winning, regardless of your manner and the title is yours.

With half the season concluded, Arsene Wenger must be wishing that he received a Christmas gift from the Arsenal medical team. Injuries have decimated his midfield with Wilshire, Cazorla, Rosiscky, Coquelin and Sanchez out of the game.

There is some good news with Mesul Ozil having managed to partake in some leisure instead of participating in the FA cup victory over Sunderland. Keeping the nimble playmaker fit would be key to Arsenal aspirations, both in this match and for the remainder of the season.

With both Petr Mertersacker and Gabriel available, it would be interesting to see whom Arsene Wenger picks out for his starting XI. Koscielny, Bellerin and Monreal have nailed down their place in the defence and the inclusion of the slower Mertersacker or the inconsistent Gabriel may have a defining moment in the game.

With Arsenal’s midfield woes, it should fall to Flamini to screen the defence with Ramsey alongside him. Walcott, Ozil and Joel Campbell should be the main thrusts of Arsenal’s attacking play with Giroud as the elegant, decisive focus.

Probable Starting XI (4-5-1): Cech; Bellerin, Gabriel, Koscielny, Monreal; Flamini, Ramsey, Ozil, Walcott, Campbell; Girourd.

With previous encounters between these teams resulting in high scoring draws, we favour a repeat of last year’s epic 2-2 result for the same fixture. Martin Skrtel’s 97th minute header in front of the Kop capped a memorable game which also had Fabio Borini sent off and we expect similar fireworks at Anfield tomorrow.

#1728. GdS: Milan ready €50m January assault for Tresoldi to give Ramos a partner – the strategy

AC Milan are serious about signing Nicolo Tresoldi from Club Brugge, with an attempt being readied ahead of the winter window.

According to La Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan intend to sign another striker even before the summer arrives, in order to boost their Champions League hopes. The name that they have chosen is someone the fans already know well: Nicolo Tresoldi.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

At the end of June, the club announced the signing of Gonçalo Ramos for over €70m, the most expensive signing in the club’s history to date (and likely for a while to come). Ramos hasn’t – at least for now – cured Milan’s goal-scoring deficiency in the No.9 role.

The negotiations for Tresoldi, however, are shaping up to be costly. Last summer, Club Brugge rejected another Italian offer of €35m from Roma, and in the meantime the price has skyrocketed after the forward bagged 13 goals in 15 games.

Adding his four goals this season against Germany’s youth team brings him close to 20 for the season already. His league hat-trick against VV Sint-Truiden at the end of October followed his hat-trick at San Siro against Inter, marking the night that every Rossoneri fan knew his name.

Therefore, the cost could now be around €50m, another huge expense if Milan really decide to go all-in. The club made a €24m loss in the last accounts after three years of profit, and the temptation is to speculate to accumulate, i.e. to invest more and make sure of the Champions League revenues.

There’s a desire to finalise the deal as early as the January transfer window, unless Brugge move to raise the price, perhaps due to a potential foreign competition. Milan believe that their relationship with the Belgian side is actually strong, with Gerry Cardinale ready to lead talks again.

As for Ramos, the investment so far has yielded just three goals and two assists, which doesn’t mean he wasn’t effective and is ready to be shelved, but it’s precisely when paired with another striker that the management believes the Portuguese could be more productive.

In short, a two-striker team can’t be ruled out in the future, with Tresoldi alongside the former Benfica man. In the European race goals fuel the climb, and Milan know this after last season’s late collapse, keen to avoid it again.

Should Milan hit a wall erected by Club Brugge, they would leave the Tresoldi option open for the summer. In the meantime, they would fill the gap with a striker on loan from a top European club.

However, Tresoldi could provide an initial assist for Milan: his support for the Rossoneri is well-known and has been publicly stated, so among the various options available, Nicolò would choose the San Siro.

A permanent return to Italy could also benefit coach Roberto Mancini, who – after the Under-21 European Championship (which Tresoldi will compete in with Germany) – would finally like him to play for the senior Azzurri side.

Nicolò, born in Cagliari in August 2004, is still free to choose which (senior) national team he wants to represent, and Mancini expressed his confidence earlier this week: “I spoke to Tresoldi, and Ranieri spoke to us too. First of all, I think he needs to feel the desire to play for Italy.

“He was born in Italy, like his father [former defender Emanuele], who played for the Under-21s and won the European Championship. I think there’s a chance he’ll choose the Azzurri. He knows he can be an important player for our future, and I hope he makes the right choice.”

#1727. Mauricio Pochettino to Man United: How the Glazer family flexed their muscles to secure Argentine's arrival at Old Trafford

By Matt Law | 12 Nov 2026 20:20, Last updated: 12 Nov 2026 20:24

The Glazer family reportedly rejected the idea of Eddie Howe becoming Manchester United's new head coach, with the club's majority owners intervening to push Mauricio Pochettino to the top of the managerial shortlist.

Man United sacked Michael Carrick as head coach on Thursday morning, with the Englishman paying the price for the team's poor start to the campaign.

According to the Daily Mail, Man United's director of football Jason Wilcox and the club's CEO Omar Berrada had been pushing for Howe to arrive at Old Trafford.

However, the report claims that the Glazers rejected Howe's arrival and instead insisted that Pochettino should be the number one choice.

Berrada and Wilcox were therefore allegedly both overruled, with the Glazers confident that Pochettino is the best choice at this moment in time.

Pochettino is expected to take charge of USA's two matches during this international period against Haiti before officially beginning work at Man United next Thursday.

As a result, the Argentine will have incredibly limited preparation time for Man United's Premier League clash with Liverpool at Anfield on November 22.

The Glazer family remain in control of the biggest decisions at the club rather than INEOS.

Avram Glazer reportedly signed off on Pochettino's appointment on Wednesday, with Man United agreeing to pay in the region of £7.4m to release the South American from his contract with the USA, which is due to run until 2030.

Avram, who is Man United's co-chairman, is said to have confirmed the decision via a remote call on Wednesday evening, as he is in the United States.

As well as Howe, Antonio Conte was heavily linked with the role, in addition to Julian Nagelsmann, with all three currently out of work.

However, Pochettino's arrival is now all but confirmed, and Man United will be hopeful that the 54-year-old can help the 20-time English champions return to former glories.
